Significant-bias threshold: Total allowable error (TAE) 15% and reference change value (RCV) 18.6% (normal level) / 22.8% (high level) for PT (Table 1); statistical significance P < .05
Sample type: Citrated plasma; 3.6-mL plastic vacuum tubes containing 3.2% buffered sodium citrate (Sarstedt); 10 healthy volunteers and 10 patients on oral vitamin K antagonist therapy
Study method details: Venous blood drawn with a syringe system and immediately transferred without any order into tubes to give fill rates of 100%, 90%, 80%, 70%, 60% and 50% (2.7, 2.4, 2.1, 1.8, 1.5 and 1.2 mL blood); tubes mixed by slow end-over-end inversion; analysed immediately after centrifugation (10 min, 2000 g, room temperature); results evaluated against total allowable error and reference change value as well as by Mann-Whitney U test
Additional sources of bias: Blood drawn with a syringe system and transferred into tubes rather than collected by direct vacuum underfill; only 20 participants and only one class of oral anticoagulant (vitamin K antagonist); findings are specific to the Sarstedt tube brand and the Stago reagent/analyzer combination; the authors state a larger study is needed before adopting the thresholds; results are labelled "PT, s" throughout the tables although the Methods describe "International normalized PT"

Significant-bias threshold: 15% bias ("94% of all PT sample pairs had a bias of less than 15%"); analyser default QNS setting = 90% fill threshold
Clinical significance vs user APS: Significant — 3.1% (reported, magnitude of the -3.1% average bias between redrawn and QNS PT) exceeds user APS 2%
Sample type: Citrated plasma; routine clinical PT samples flagged QNS by the CS-5100 default settings and redrawn within 4 hours
Study method details: Retrospective study over a 12-week period; approximately 13,000 PT and PTT tests performed; for PT, 139 samples were QNS and 108 were redrawn within 4 hours (average time to redraw 66 minutes, range 23-228); relative bias between redrawn and original results evaluated against time between draws, tube fill, sex, age and haematocrit
Additional sources of bias: Retrospective paired design in which the comparator is a later redraw rather than a simultaneous correctly filled tube (average 66 minutes apart, up to 228 minutes), so biological change between draws is not excluded; tube fill expressed as probe travel distance in mm rather than as a percentage fill; meeting abstract with no tables or per-fill-level data; no INR reported
Notes: Meeting abstract. The sign convention for "bias between redrawn and QNS PT" is not defined in the abstract, so the raw Direction of effect and the user-APS direction are the missing literal; only the magnitude is transcribed. Conclusion: "the default tube fill settings on the CS-5100 were overly restrictive for PT; decreasing the tube fill requirement by 10 mm would prevent 93% of PT rejections due to QNS yet still yield accurate results".
